  • One Stop, Three Races, No Invented All-Clear [Part 1/4]: Suppose a safety monitor engages a machine stop after an autonomous worker begins behaving anomalously. Three races now matter, and none can be resolved by a dashboard toggle: A project-scoped stop follows the same latch and recovery discipline without revoking unrelated… — Key Rules/Claims: Containment races cleanup. The latch reaches durable storage before AINA attempts to terminate owned runs or cancel queued wakes. One worker termination remains unconfirmed; the latch still closes new effects.
  • 1. Asymmetric Containment [Part 1/4]: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.1 — Stop versus recovery authority — The emergency interface deliberately gives stop and recovery different authority. Any admitted caller may invoke engage because refusal to stop is the more dangerous default. A nonempty reason is mandatory. — Key Rules/Claims: No MCP session. If session::current() exists, recovery is refused. A model-connected tool session cannot satisfy the owner surface. | Explicit operator identity. The caller must supply --by operator; a worker or agent name is insufficient.
  • 2. Latch-First Containment [Part 1/4]: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.2 — Publication before cleanup; Exhibit 8.3 — Sanitized scoped latch record; Owned Jobs must be observed stopped; “Latched” is not the same as “fully reconciled” — An emergency stop must not depend on a database, a live server, a lease sweep, a successful process kill, or a final audit write. Those steps can fail precisely when containment is needed. The distinction matters. — Spec/Table: KILLING: An affected owned Job is not yet observed quiescent, a Job census failed, or a live server does not implement the current break-glass observation protocol. | RECONCILING: Quiescence and protocol coverage are established, but an unresolved file, destination, or model operation remains—or its registry cannot be read.

Control Epochs Revoke Authority, Not Just Processes [Part 2/4]: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.4 — Scoped revocation map; WAL before snapshot; Exhibit 8.5 — Sanitized epoch-advance record — A latch closes new-effect gates immediately. Control epochs handle a different problem: authority that was minted before the stop must not remain usable after the relevant boundary advances. — Spec/Table: Resource lease; Carried lineage: Lease.control_epoch; Recheck at the boundary: validate_tenancy checks expiry, current generation, and matching scope revision | Room wake job; Carried lineage: sealed control_epoch; Recheck at the boundary: Dispatch re-derives task/Room/project standing and refuses revoked lineage | Result-grant receiving tenancy; Carried lineage: Recipient.control_epoch; Recheck… — Key Rules/Claims: Reads the current epoch and per-scope revisions. | Computes next = prior + 1, refusing integer exhaustion. | Appends an epoch_advance record to breakglass.wal.jsonl and flushes it. | Atomically rewrites epoch.json with the new sequence and scope map. | Reads the epoch back and refuses an unconfirmed result.

Managed Drain and In-Doubt Recovery [Part 2/4]: Subtopics: Recovery starts with a census, not amnesia; Exhibit 8.6 — Recovery intent preserves uncertainty; Stop beats recovery on a race; Exhibit 8.7 — Racing stop leaves FROZEN_SAFE — Immediate engage is not the only controlled-stop mode. drain supports a bounded window in which already durably prepared effects may finish. It requires the same owner console and an already-engaged machine latch, so new effects are refused before the drain begins. — Key Rules/Claims: unresolved_file_operations() for protected file writes without an established outcome; | destinations::unresolved_operations() for nonterminal destination mutations; | model_egress::unresolved() for brokered model requests whose provider-side outcome is unsettled.

The Candidate-Binary Publication Gate [Part 3/4]: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.8 — Candidate qualification sequence; The complete 45-case inventory — Containment architecture is only as credible as the binary that implements it. A green build proves compilation. It does not prove that the release artifact refuses stale generations, impersonation, cross-project reads, altered proposals, damaged recovery objects, or evidence… — Spec/Table: 1; Emitted case ID: impersonation_refused; What must hold: A bound session cannot act as another owner. | 2; Emitted case ID: altered_proposal_conflict; What must hold: Reusing an operation ID with a different payload is refused. | 3; Emitted case ID: stale_generation_refused; What must hold: An edit fencing an old ownership generation is rejected.
  • 6. What the Gate Proves—and What It Cannot [Part 3/4]: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.9 — Publication summary shape — The release gate closes an important bootstrapping hole. The candidate carries its own inventory and enforcement code, the surface receipt binds the expected harness and target image hashes, and the source digest is checked before and after a potentially long run. — Spec/Table: Rust IsTerminal / console handles; What it establishes: Whether standard handles belong to a terminal; What AINA adds—and refuses to infer: Combines terminal detection with no MCP session, explicit operator identity, and OS confinement; terminal presence alone is not human identity.
